# Web Search and Retrieval Strategies for Agents

Covers live web search vs RAG vs hybrid approaches, multi-hop retrieval, iteration counts, diminishing returns, and source inaccessibility.

For source details, see [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Live Web Search vs RAG vs Hybrid

| Approach | Strengths | Weaknesses | Best For |
|----------|-----------|------------|----------|
| Traditional RAG | Fast, cheap, single-pass | Struggles with multi-hop, stale knowledge | Simple lookup queries |
| Live web search | Current information, broad coverage | Slow, expensive, source accessibility issues | Time-sensitive research |
| Agentic RAG (hybrid) | Dynamic routing, adaptive iteration | Higher token cost, complexity | Complex research with mixed query types |

RAG reduces hallucination from ~40% to 0-6% in domain-specific applications with reliable sources [15], but at a response rate cost of 19-64% (the system declines questions where retrieval is insufficient) [15].

The industry is converging on "Agentic RAG" — a hybrid where an LLM agent dynamically chooses between local retrieval, web search, and structured queries based on query complexity [15], [22].

## Multi-Hop Retrieval

Multi-hop retrieval follows a search → decompose → retrieve → reason → retrieve cycle. Complex queries are broken into atomic sub-queries executed sequentially or in parallel.

The Search-R1 study found a fundamental trade-off: "allocating more tokens to search reduces the capacity available for reasoning, and vice versa" [23]. This is task-dependent — literature surveys benefit from search-heavy allocation, while causal analysis benefits from reasoning-heavy allocation [23].

**Counter-intuitive finding**: Longer explicit reasoning degrades performance in deep research agents. The Search-R1 "fast thinking" template (direct search/answer decisions without intermediate reasoning blocks) outperforms "slow thinking" (explicit reasoning before each action) [23].

## Iteration Counts and Diminishing Returns

### RAG + CoT Performance
RAG + CoT using GPT-3.5-Turbo achieved the lowest hallucination rate of 11% on HaluEval [22]. "Combining RAG and CoT outperforms individual methods, mainly because retrieval provides factual grounding while CoT guides step-by-step reasoning" [22].

### Self-Consistency
Self-consistency with 9 samples at varied temperature (0.3-0.7) achieves ~80% accuracy on TruthfulQA and ~90% on FEVER [22].

### Adaptive vs Fixed Iteration
No single "optimal number" of iterations exists. Adaptive strategies that scale iterations based on query complexity are recommended. The Search-R1 study [23] shows that letting the model decide when to stop outperforms fixed-iteration approaches.

### Practical Guidance
The Anthropic multi-agent system uses explicit scaling rules: simple fact-finding → 3-10 tool calls; direct comparisons → 10-15 calls per subagent; complex research → divide across 10+ subagents [1]. This reduces research time by up to 90% for complex queries [1].

### Content Drift
Beyond complete inaccessibility: 13% of intact NYT links had significantly drifted content — the page loads but the content changed materially [13]. This is a distinct problem for citation integrity that standard link-checking misses.

### AI Crawler Blocking
- Over 1 million Cloudflare customers have blocked AI crawlers since September 2024 [27]
- Cloudflare powers approximately 20% of the web [27]
- This creates a growing inaccessibility layer specifically targeting automated research agents

### Wikipedia
- 54% of Wikipedia pages have broken references [7]
- 11% of reference links are inaccessible [7]

## Handling Inaccessible Sources

**Practical strategies** (derived from methodology observations):
1. Provide 2-3 candidate sources per data point
2. Use academic databases (Semantic Scholar, CrossRef) as fallbacks for DOI-bearing sources
3. Search for paper titles + specific data points when PDFs fail
4. Check PubMed abstracts for summary data when full papers are inaccessible
5. Record all failures visibly — never silently drop sources
6. Above 50% inaccessibility signals the topic may lack accessible web sources [methodology note]

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No study measures real-time agent inaccessibility rates**: Link rot studies measure historical decay, not the failure rate an agent encounters when fetching URLs from fresh search results. The actual rate for a CLI research agent is unmeasured.
- **PDF extraction success rates**: No quantitative data found on how often PDF extraction specifically fails vs HTML fetching.
- **Cloudflare block rates for LLM agents specifically**: 1M+ customers blocking [27] and ~20% web coverage [27] suggests significant impact, but no study measures the actual experienced block rate.
- **Content drift detection**: Most tools check only for HTTP status codes, not for whether content has changed since citation — a gap for long-running research projects.
